public_rationale: Marcus says Grok misread his terse question and described a recent Billings earthquake that, from his fact-checking, did not happen. The part public records can check holds. The USGS catalog for December 2024 through 20 February 2025, within 200 km of Billings at magnitude 2 or above, lists only eight events. All are classified as mining explosions, and none is an earthquake. So no recent Billings quake of note occurred, and any account of one was fabricated. What Grok actually said is known only from Marcus's screenshots, which I take as described but cannot verify independently.
limitations: The rating depends on the verifiable part (no quake). Grok's actual output is not independently documented.
The 200 km radius and the window starting 2024-12-01 are my reading of 'there' and 'recently'.
The catalog was queried through the USGS API. Its reviewed records were last updated in 2025-04.

our_interpretation: Reading: the checkable core is whether Billings, Montana, had a recent earthquake before 2025-02-19 of the kind Grok described. If public seismic records show no such quake, the earthquake Grok reported was fabricated.
'Recently' is taken as the roughly 2.5 months before the post (2024-12-01 to 2025-02-19). The search area is 200 km around Billings, at magnitude 2 or more.
What Grok actually said is documented only in Marcus's screenshots. That part is taken as he described it and is not independently verified.
criteria.support_condition: Authoritative seismic catalogs (USGS) show no earthquake near Billings in the weeks before 2025-02-19.
criteria.contradiction_condition: USGS or other authoritative records show a notable earthquake at or near Billings shortly before 2025-02-19, or an independent record shows Grok never described such a quake.
